formationLabel: Organized from All Saints in 1913 · Lithuanian parish worship began 15 February 1914 · Emerald church opened 6 December 1914 · Halsted church dedicated 31 May 1959 · extinguished by union effective 1 July 2022
currentUse: The Ss. Peter and Paul juridic parish was extinguished effective July 1, 2022 and united with Holy Name of Mary and St. John de La Salle into a newly erected territorial parish. Holy Name of Mary Church was designated the new parish church. The former Ss. Peter and Paul church at 12433–12439 S. Halsted was documented standing by CTA in 2022 and marketed as a church complex in 2023; its ownership, occupancy, worship use, and present structural/interior condition after that listing are unresolved.
summary: Ss. Peter and Paul was the Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish organized in Chicago's West Pullman district in 1913 from All Saints, not either of Chicago's other same-name parishes. Lithuanian parishioners first worshiped at Assumption BVM at 123rd and Parnell in February 1914, then moved to a combination church-school at 12255 S. Emerald in December 1914. A new Mid-Century Modern church was built in 1958 at 12433–12439 S. Halsted and dedicated in May 1959, proving that the inherited 1959 value is a building milestone rather than parish formation. Wolkovich's 1973 consolidation reading cannot be an institutional closure because the Archdiocese's 2022 decree names Ss. Peter and Paul as a continuing juridic person. That decree extinguished it effective July 1, 2022 and united it with two parishes to create a new territorial successor whose parish church is Holy Name of Mary. The Halsted building stood in 2022–2023, but its current use remains unresolved.

institutionLifecycle.formation: Organized in late 1913 from All Saints; Lithuanian parish worship began at Assumption BVM on 15 February 1914. The 30 July 1914 cornerstone report and December 1914 church opening are building milestones.
institutionLifecycle.jurisdiction: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago; founded as a Lithuanian national parish and later served a broader territorial community.
institutionLifecycle.ethnicStatusTransition: Wolkovich reports a 23 February 1973 consolidation, but the exact instrument and effect are unresolved. It was not juridic extinction because the 2022 decree treats Ss. Peter and Paul as an existing parish.
institutionLifecycle.terminalStatus: Extinguished as a separate juridic person and united into a newly erected territorial parish effective 1 July 2022.

historicalNarrative.text: This case is the Lithuanian Ss. Peter and Paul parish of West Pullman, not the Polish parish on Paulina Street or the German parish at 91st and Exchange. Wolkovich traces it to All Saints and says it formed in 1913. Parish registers begin in January 1914, and the parish history reports that Rev. Norbert Lukošius began organizing in late 1913. The inherited 1959 founding value is therefore untenable as an institutional date.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, vol. 3, pp. 147–148

historicalNarrative.text: Before its own church opened, the Lithuanian parish worshiped at the Polish Assumption BVM Church at 123rd and Parnell from February 15 through November 30, 1914. Its combination church-school at 12255 South Emerald was then used from December 6, 1914. The Archdiocesan locations register gives November 29 as the building milestone, while the parish-anniversary account distinguishes dedication from first usable worship on December 6; both belong to the first parish building, not parish formation.

historicalNarrative.text: The later Halsted church explains the misleading 1958/1959 dates. CTA's technical survey identifies the Mid-Century Modern church at 12433–12439 South Halsted as built in 1958 and describes its physical fabric. Parish history dates dedication to May 31, 1959. The church replaced the Emerald worship site while the same parish continued; CTA also records a minor address conflict, with another agency using 12427 for the same building.

historicalNarrative.text: Wolkovich reports a consolidation on February 23, 1973. That cannot be treated as juridic closure: Archdiocesan decree Prot. N. 2022 RMC-12 expressly names Ss. Peter and Paul as one of three existing parishes to be extinguished in 2022. The 1973 event is therefore retained as an unresolved ethnic or administrative transition, consistent with the parish's later broader community, rather than flattened into an institutional end.

sources.locator: Archdiocese decree Prot. N. 2022 RMC-12, PDF/printed p. 3, clauses 1–5

historicalNarrative.text: The controlling terminal event is an extinctive union effective July 1, 2022. The decree extinguished Ss. Peter and Paul, Holy Name of Mary, and St. John de La Salle as separate juridic persons, erected one new territorial parish, transferred ministries, parishioners, goods, rights, and obligations, and designated Holy Name of Mary Church as parish church. CTA documented the Halsted church as standing in 2022 and a 2023 listing offered the complex for sale, but no later source proves current ownership, worship, or structural/interior condition.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The inherited 1959 founding value is the dedication year of the second permanent church, while institution formation belongs to 1913–1914. Wolkovich's 1973 consolidation reading cannot be juridic closure because the Archdiocese extinguished the still-existing parish in 2022. The inherited 2022 terminal reading is correct only when described as extinctive union into a newly erected parish, not a simple building closure. The contaminated phrase 'Coal region' is excluded.
